newsitem.title: USA: Jones says truth will out in Clinton sex encounter.
newsitem.headline: Jones says truth will out in Clinton sex encounter.

text.p: A woman suing President Bill Clinton for sexual harassment said on Sunday she would have never pursued the case this far if she were lying.
"If I could get, get to trial, I'm sure that, that the truth would come out," Paula Corbin Jones told CBS "60 Minutes" in an interview.

Jones has filed a sexual harassment suit against Clinton seeking $700,000 in damages. She claims he made improper sexual advances to her and sought oral sex after he summoned her to a room in the Excelsior Hotel in Little Rock, Ark., on May 8, 1991 when he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state-employed clerk.

Clinton has made no public comment on the Jones case. But his lawyer, Robert Bennett, argued before the U.S. Supreme Court in January that a sexual harassment lawsuit should be put on hold until Clinton left office because it would distract him from his presidential duties.
Attorneys for Jones replied the president should not be placed above the law.
A ruling -- solely on the procedural issue of whether the case may proceed immediately, not on its merits -- is expected before the Supreme Court ends its current session in June.
Also in the "60 Minutes" program on Sunday was Arkansas State Trooper Danny Ferguson who brought Jones to Clinton's hotel room.

Ferguson, who is the target of a second suit by Jones accused her in the program of lying, but Jones retorted: "I'm not lying, I'm telling the truth. And I would have never taken it this far if I was lying."

Ferguson told "60 Minutes" that after Jones left Clinton's hotel room, she asked him if Clinton had a girlfriend. When Ferguson replied "no", she allegedly said "well, I'll be his girlfriend if he wants one."

But Jones retorted: "Now, why would I say that? If it went so well in that room, that hotel room, why wouldn't I tell the Governor myself? Why would I go hunt down his bodyguard or whatever, to tell him that I wanted to be his regular girlfriend? Now isn't that kind of stupid?"

Asked by "60 Minutes" interviewer Ed Bradley what she wanted from Clinton, Jones said: "An apology. And it's as simple as that. I want an apology, because he was, well, he did something wrong to me. And I want my reputation back, and the lies to stop, and an apology."
